property_summary: In M, after calling go(), the contract's balance is zero regardless of any prior external deposit, whereas in P, go() transfers the contract's full balance to owner, which can be non-zero if prior deposits were made into the contract.
In P, go() always reverts when called, whereas in M, go() succeeds and transfers the contract's entire balance to the owner.
In P go() always reverts when called with a non-zero amount, while in M go() always succeeds for the same call.

After go() executes, either the external call succeeded (and balance is 0) or it failed (and the reference reverts while the mutant does not), so the reference never leaves the contract with a positive balance.

After any call to go(), the contract's balance must be zero in the reference because it either reverts on external call failure or transfers all remaining balance to the owner; the mutant skips the require, so when the external call fails it proceeds to transfer the original balance but leaves any new deposit unhandled, resulting in a non-zero balance.
